- `launch` — Launch a new browser process. headless: true for headless mode (default), false for visible window. Returns Err if Chrome is not installed or cannot be started.
- `new_page` — Create a new page (tab) in this browser.
- `capture_console` — Opt this page into console/error capture.  `drain_events("console", …)` and `on_console` need it; network events do not. It sends Runtime.enable, which anti-bot systems can detect, so it is not automatic. `on_console`, `on_error`, `expose_function` and `expose_binding` call it themselves.
- `goto` — Navigate to a URL and wait for page load. This is the correct way to access JS-rendered pages. For HTTP-only requests (no JS), use fetch() instead.
- `navigate` — Navigate to a URL (alias for goto).
- `goto_antibot` — Anti-bot-aware navigation. Routes through the AntiBotOrchestrator so proxy selection/rotation, rate limiting, cookie farming, and CAPTCHA handling actually drive egress (relaunching the browser on the chosen proxy) instead of the raw `page.navigate` used by `goto`.  Optional second argument — a per-call egress/stealth map: {proxy: String, tor: Bool, stealth: Bool, tier: String} - proxy:    explicit proxy URL for THIS navigation ("socks5://…", "http://…"). Wins over the orchestrator's own selection. - tor:      true routes this navigation through Tor instances (implies per-domain circuit isolation). - stealth:  stealth on the relaunched browser (default true). - tier:     "tor" | "direct" | "datacenter" | "residential" | "isp" | "mobile". Classifies `proxy`, or "direct" pins this navigation to direct egress (no Tor fallback attempts). With no map, historical behavior applies (default Tor fallback pool + NOT wired on either plane: there is no interp arm and no native lowering. The orchestrator itself exists in Rust (src/browser/antibot.rs, invoked from src/stdlib/browser.rs) — what is missing is the per-plane dispatch. See docs/browser-native-gaps.md.
- `title` — Get the current page title.
- `url` — Get the current page URL.
- `content` — Full HTML of the current document, serialized from the live DOM (post-JS), not the bytes the server sent.
- `set_content` — Replace the document with `html`. The current DOM is discarded; the page handle stays bound, so later navigation still works.
- `wait_for_timeout` — Sleep for `ms`. Explicit wait; `elapsed_ms` reports what actually elapsed rather than echoing the request.
- `wait_for_function` — Poll a JS expression until it is truthy or `timeout_ms` elapses (default 30000). A timeout is `result: false`, not an error.
- `wait_for_url` — Wait until `location.href` matches `pattern` (`*` wildcards).
- `wait_for_event` — Wait for a CDP event — full method (`Page.loadEventFired`) or bare name (`loadEventFired`). Subscribe before the triggering action: events are not replayed.
- `wait_for_request` — Wait for an outgoing request whose URL matches `pattern`.
- `wait_for_response` — Wait for a response whose URL matches `pattern`.
- `add_init_script` — Run `script` before every document in this page loads.
- `add_script_tag` — Append a <script> to the current document. A value with a scheme is treated as a URL, anything else as inline source.
- `add_style_tag` — Append a <style> to the current document; same URL/contents rule.
- `emulate_media` — Emulate media type, colour scheme and reduced-motion preference.
- `emulate_vision` — Emulate a vision deficiency (none, blurredVision, deuteranopia, …).
- `throttle_network` — Apply a network preset: slow-3g, fast-3g, 4g or none. An unknown preset is an error, never a silent no-op.
- `on_console` — Register a `.tl` handler for page events. Delivery is deferred: the handler runs at the start of the next Page method call, with a `PageEvent` argument.
- `on_error` — Uncaught page errors (window.onerror / unhandled rejections).
- `on_request` — Outgoing network requests.
- `on_response` — Network responses.
- `on_filechooser` — File chooser dialogs.
- `on_download` — Download events.
- `expose_function` — Expose a JS function `name` that calls the `.tl` handler with the binding payload. Calls are buffered and delivered on the next Page call.
- `expose_binding` — Like `expose_function`, for bindings that also receive caller context.
- `drain_events` — Drain buffered page events, oldest first. `kind` empty means every category; `limit` 0 means all currently buffered. Taking removes them.
- `throttle_cpu` — Slow the CPU by `rate` (1.0 native, 4.0 = 4x slower).
- `query_selector` — Find the first element matching a CSS selector. Returns Err if no element matches.
- `query_selector_all` — Find all elements matching a CSS selector. Returns empty array if no elements match.
- `wait_for_selector` — Wait for an element matching the selector to appear in the DOM. Returns Err on timeout.
- `fill` — Fill a form field by CSS selector: focus, clear, then type the value character-by-character (real CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent). clear_first defaults to true; delay_ms paces the keystrokes.
- `click` — Click the element matching a CSS selector (auto-waits actionability, scrolls into view, dispatches Input.dispatchMouseEvent).
- `select` — Select an <option> inside the <select> matching a CSS selector. by: "value" (default) | "label" | "index"; option is the match target.
- `resolve_antibot` — Detect → solve → retry orchestration over the page's CURRENT egress (ROADMAP #9). Sequences captcha.detect, the external-solver solve leg (incl. Turnstile), warmup/escalation capability flags, and a bounded re-navigation, returning an AntibotResolveReport whose per-engine steps carry honest {engine, available, ran, note} capability flags. Optional opts map: {solver_key: String, solver_service: String}.
- `reload` — Reload the current page.
- `go_back` — Navigate back in history.
- `go_forward` — Navigate forward in history.
- `scroll_by` — Scroll by pixel amounts.
- `scroll_to_bottom` — Scroll to the bottom of the page.
- `get_cookies` — Extract all browser cookies via CDP Network.getCookies. Returns an array of CdpCookie structs.
- `cookie_string` — Generate a Cookie header string for the given URL from the browser's cookie jar. Filters cookies by domain match, returns "name=value; name2=value2".
- `set_cookies_from_header` — Set cookies in the browser from a Cookie header string. domain: the domain to set cookies for (e.g. "ghraonline.com") path: the cookie path (default "/")
- `authenticated_get` — Make an authenticated HTTP GET request using browser cookies. Extracts cookies from the browser and sends via ureq through the runtime egress contract (proxy-aware; Tor by default) with a Cookie header. Returns {status: Int, body: String}.
- `authenticated_request` — Make an authenticated HTTP request with browser cookies. method: "GET", "POST", etc. body: request body string. Returns {status: Int, body: String}.
- `page_is_wordfence_challenge` — Check if the current page is a Wordfence JS challenge page ("One moment, please...").
- `page_bypass_wordfence` — Bypass the Wordfence JS challenge on the current page. Executes the challenge JS and waits for auto-redirect. Returns the final URL after bypass.
- `page_navigate_bypass_wordfence` — Navigate to a URL automatically bypassing Wordfence if encountered. Combines page.goto() + wordfence detection + auto-bypass.
- `page_wp_extract_rest_nonce` — Extract the WordPress REST API nonce (wp_rest) from the current page. Returns nil if not found (not logged in, or not an admin page).
- `page_wp_is_logged_in` — Check if the browser is currently logged into WordPress. Detects admin bar, logged-in body class, or logout links.
- `page_wp_login` — Attempt WordPress login via wp-login.php form. Navigates to login page, fills form, submits, detects outcome. Returns LoginResult with status: "success", "2fa_required", "failed", or "unknown".
- `page_wp_extract_all_nonces` — Extract ALL WordPress nonces from the current page. Returns array of WpNonce structs (REST, admin, etc.).

- `create` — Create a browser pool with max_size instances.  Optional trailing args: `headless` (default true) and an egress/stealth map `{proxy, tor, stealth, tier}`: - proxy:   proxy URL for the pool's browsers ("socks5://…", "http://…"). Wins over the TALLOW_PROXY env var. - tor:     true routes pool browsers through Tor instances (3), like TALLOW_TOR=1. - stealth: stealth flags on each pool browser launch. - tier:    "tor" | "direct" | "datacenter" | "residential" | "isp" | "mobile". Classifies `proxy` explicitly; "direct" is an explicit choice of direct egress (no env inheritance, no leak warning). Keys omitted from the map fall back to TALLOW_PROXY / TALLOW_TOR. Without any egress the pool launches DIRECT and warns (real-IP leak risk). Real arm: interp.rs BrowserPool.create; per-instance egress is resolved in pool.rs resolve_proxy and applied to BrowserConfig.proxy (Chrome's --proxy-server flag).

```tallow
fn gunzip(data: Bytes) -> Result<Bytes> { decompress_with(data, algo: .Gzip) }
```

<a id="jobs"></a>
## `jobs`

```tallow
fn submit(name: String, script: String, schedule_spec: String, opts: Map?) -> String
fn list() -> [ScheduledJob]
fn pause(id: String) -> Bool
fn resume(id: String) -> Bool
fn remove(id: String) -> Bool
fn run_now(id: String) -> String
fn status(id: String) -> JobStatus
fn set_max_concurrent(n: Int) -> Bool
fn get_max_concurrent() -> Int
```

- `submit` — Submit a new job. The job id is its unique name (duplicates are rejected). Returns the job id.  Optional 4th arg (a Map): {max_parallel: n} caps how many instances of this job may run concurrently (clamped 1..256, persisted on the job). Extra map keys are ignored.
- `list` — List all jobs in the store as ScheduledJob structs.
- `pause` — Pause a job by id (it will not fire until resumed). Errors on unknown id.
- `resume` — Resume a paused job by id; recomputes next_run. Errors on unknown id.
- `remove` — Remove a job by id. Errors on unknown id.
- `run_now` — Run a job's script once right now, as a subprocess (`tallow run`), and record the outcome (last_status/last_run/run_count) when it finishes. Async: returns "running" when spawned, "queued" when the concurrency cap is full (the request is queued FIFO and starts as slots free up). Real errors (no fake success) when the job or its script file does not exist. Poll jobs.status(id) until "done" to observe completion.
- `status` — Run-state of one job: idle | pending | running | done plus counters. Errors on unknown id.
- `set_max_concurrent` — Persist the store-wide concurrency cap (clamped 1..256). Survives restarts via the ScheduleStore JSON. Initial default: TALLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT env var, else 40 (same as the scheduler daemon).
- `get_max_concurrent` — Effective store-wide concurrency cap (persisted value, else the TALLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT env var, else 40).

- `read_audit_log` — Read audit log entries back from the JSONL audit log (default TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR/audit_log.jsonl when path is empty)
- `consent_register` — Record explicit consent (GDPR Art.6/7, CCPA) — appends to TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR/consent_register.jsonl and returns a record id
- `consent_check` — True iff the consent register holds a current registration for the subject + purpose pair
- `erasure_request` — Log a GDPR right-to-erasure request (Art.17) — appends to TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR/erasure_requests.jsonl and returns a request id
- `subject_access_request` — Log a GDPR subject-access request (Art.15) — same register as erasure requests, distinct event type; returns a request id
- `generate_report` — Generate compliance report
- `check_compliance` — Check compliance for jurisdiction
- `cra_audit` — Generate CRA compliance report for the current project
- `nis2_audit` — Generate NIS2 Art.21 compliance report
- `dora_incident_new` — Create a new ICT incident with auto-generated ID and timestamp
- `dora_classify` — Auto-classify incident severity per DORA RTS criteria CRITICAL: critical_function_impaired AND (duration > 24h OR records > 100K) HIGH:     critical_function_impaired OR clients > 10% OR records > 5,000 MEDIUM:   clients > 1% OR duration > 2h OR cross_border LOW:      all other incidents
- `dora_report` — Generate DORA-compliant incident report JSON for regulatory notification
- `ai_inference_log_create` — Create a new inference log for an AI system
- `ai_inference_log_entry` — Log an inference event (input hashed for privacy)
- `ai_inference_log_verify` — Verify log integrity (recompute hash chain)
- `ai_inference_log_export` — Export log as JSON for Art.12 audit
- `human_approval_request` — Request human approval for a high-risk decision (Art.14)
- `model_provenance_create` — Create a new model provenance record
- `model_provenance_set` — Set a provenance field (immutable update)
- `model_provenance_attest` — Attest provenance with BLAKE3 cryptographic hash
- `model_provenance_verify` — Verify attestation integrity
- `model_provenance_export` — Export provenance as JSON (for Annex IV documentation)

<a id="provenance"></a>
## `provenance`

```tallow
fn record(source_url: String, egress_label: String, egress_tier: String, status_code: Int, body_hash: String) -> CollectionRecord
fn record_at(source_url: String, egress_label: String, egress_tier: String, status_code: Int, body_hash: String, fetched_at: Int) -> CollectionRecord
fn add_validator(rec: CollectionRecord, validator: String, passed: Bool, adjustment: Float, note: String?) -> CollectionRecord
fn grade(rec: CollectionRecord) -> CollectionRecord
fn freshness(rec: CollectionRecord) -> String
fn hash_body(body: String) -> String
fn to_json(rec: CollectionRecord) -> String
fn from_json(json: String) -> CollectionRecord
```

- `record` — Create a record. fetched_at defaults to now; base confidence defaults to 0.8. Optional trailing args: fetched_at (Int), base_confidence (Float).
- `record_at` — Create a record with an explicit fetch timestamp (unix epoch seconds).
- `add_validator` — Append a validation step (passed adds |adjustment|, failed subtracts it).
- `grade` — Recompute confidence over the validator chain and assign the letter grade. Rubric: 200 = A, other 2xx = B, 3xx = C, 4xx = D, 5xx/none = F; downgraded by egress tier (datacenter/proxy −1, tor −2), confidence (< 0.7 −1, < 0.5 −2) and freshness (Stale −1, Old −2).
- `freshness` — Freshness label of a record: "Fresh" | "Recent" | "Stale" | "Old" (cutoffs < 15 min, < 6 h, < 24 h — same bands as the browser model).
- `hash_body` — sha256 hex fingerprint of a fetched body (64 lowercase hex chars).
- `to_json` — Serialize a record (incl. validators) to durable JSON.
- `from_json` — Parse a record back from the JSON produced by to_json().

- `block_key` — Coarse blocking key: Soundex(first name token) + ZIP5 of address.
- `exact` — Normalized exact-equality test for names.
- `name_similarity` — Best name similarity in [0,1]: max(Jaro–Winkler, token-set).
- `address_similarity` — Address similarity in [0,1] over canonical street forms.
- `score` — Full pairwise record score. Verdicts: match / probable / possible / weak / no.

```tallow
fn solve_turnstile(url: String) -> TurnstileSolution {
```

- `solve_turnstile` — Solve a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge on a page.  Tries the following methods in order: 1. External API (2Captcha/Anti-Captcha) — submits the Turnstile task and polls for a valid token. 2. Pre-warmed cookies — injects cf_clearance and __cf_bm cookies from the cookie farm to bypass Turnstile without solving. 3. Fresh proxy + stealth profile — rotates to a new proxy IP and launches a browser with a fresh, un-flagged stealth profile.  Returns a TurnstileSolution indicating success/failure and the method used.

<a id="warmup"></a>
## `warmup`

```tallow
fn warmup_session(url: String, level: String) -> WarmupResult {
```

- `warmup_session` — Warm up a browser session before scraping a protected domain.  level controls the warm-up intensity: - "essential": Visit homepage only (fastest, ~3-8s) - "standard": Visit 3 pages with scroll and click activity (~15-30s) - "full": Visit 10 pages with human-like browsing and Weibull timing (~60-120s)  Returns a WarmupResult containing cookies, storage, and metadata that can be injected into subsequent scraping sessions.
